column1: # The arbitrations: one row per disagreement class the gap report can raise.
# Two decoders, one encoding, two answers.  The contract's step 5 says a
# disagreement is ARBITRATED to the CORRECT output, never resolved by picking
# a side and trusting it, so each row below decides on the merits and says
# which side the merits went to.  A row is NOT a claim that the other side is
# a defect: it is a claim about what the encoding does.
#   isa       the ISA the class was measured on
#   rule      the QEMU decode rule the class sits on, or #undecoded when the
#             bytes reached no rule at all
#   qemu      the generic opcode QEMU's word maps to
#   capstone  the generic opcode the incumbent names
#   verdict   QEMU | CAPSTONE -- which side the arbitration went to
#   state     SETTLED      the tree already publishes the arbitrated answer
#             COVERAGE-PATH the arbitrated answer is not published yet and the
#                          remedy is named in the reason
#   reason    the merits, in one sentence
# THE KEY INCLUDES THE RULE ON PURPOSE.  A class keyed only on the pair of
# opcodes grows silently: x86's BITMANIP-vs-TEST class was one row when B1
# ruled it and thirty-six at a five-times-larger corpus, and a rule joining an
# already-ruled pair would have been counted as ruled without anyone reading
# it.  A new rule in an old class is a new arbitration.
# CLOSED COVERAGE PATHS.  Two rows stood here until the x86 hand statements
# landed, and they are kept as comments rather than deleted so the next
# reader can see what closed them and check it:

the witness 13001516 is addi zero,a0,0x161 -- rd IS x0, and the unprivileged spec defines ADDI with rd=x0 as a HINT, which by definition modifies no architectural state. This tree has already ruled that shape once, for the C-extension HINT code points, in the same words: a hint's register field is payload, and modelling it as work fabricates an edge onto an instruction that architecturally does nothing (champsim_tracer_decode.cc, the c.addi/c.slli64 arm). trans_addi's rd==0 arm is that rule, not an elision

the two measured encodings are c0000000 (ehb) and 40000000 (ssnop) -- the sll $0,$0,sa hint code points, which QEMU itself PRINTS as ehb and ssnop. An execution-hazard barrier and a superscalar nop perform no shift and occupy no shifter, so shl is false of them; the incumbent's nop is the closer answer and the barrier deserves better than either. REMEDY: state the hint word at OPC_SLL's rd==0 && rt==0 arm, which already exists in translate.c for the PAUSE code point

the witness is 00000000, sll $0,$0,0 -- MIPS's canonical NOP. The incumbent PRINTS nop and still maps it to SHL, which is false of it, so its answer is refused. QEMU is not right either: the corpus carries TWO rows for these bytes, one under OPC_SLL and one reaching no rule at all, so the remedy is the no-rule route and not the word

srav $0,$0,$0 is a shift whose result is written to $zero and discarded. MIPS does NOT define srav with rd=$0 as a hint -- unlike RISC-V's ADDI, where the spec says so -- so the operation happens and only the destination is architecturally inert. QEMU's word comes from gen_shift's "if no destination, treat it as a NOP" early-out, and R3/J2.3 have already ruled that shape: that is an emulation optimisation, not the architecture. REMEDY: state the shift word ABOVE the rd==0 return in gen_shift, and let the zero-destination note carry the discard

the nine witnesses are 00030000 00060000 40020000 40050000 80010000 80040000 80070000 c0030000 c0060000 -- every one of them sll $zero,$zero,sa with rs == 0, rt == 0, rd == 0 and sa in {6,9,12,15,18,21,24,27,30}. That is the MIPS32 hint code-point space, not a shift: sa 0 is NOP, 1 SSNOP, 3 EHB, 5 PAUSE, and the remaining sa values are reserved for future hints and execute as no-ops. Nothing is read (rs is $zero), nothing is written (rd is $zero), and no shifter is occupied, so the incumbent's shl -- a shift of zero by sa, delivering zero to a register that cannot hold it -- is true of no implementation. QEMU states the word at the gate that owns exactly this code-point space, translate.c:13683 (op1 == OPC_SLL and rd == rs == rt == 0), ahead of the dispatch-site rule word because note_word() is first-wins. NOTE THE SCOPE, the 221-F rule: this key can also be reached by the four NAMED hints, which AGREE at this tip (both decoders word 00000000, 40000000 and c0000000 as nop) and so are absent from the class here. For those, nop is the closer answer but not the whole one -- an execution-hazard barrier and a superscalar nop deserve their own word -- and that remedy is the standing coverage path on the OPC_SLL GEN_OP_SHL / GEN_OP_NOP row above. The state is carried as COVERAGE-PATH so this row stays true if the named hints ever join the class; for the nine reserved hints measured here nothing further is owed

fld m32fp/m80fp (flds d90565fa1700, fldt db28 and 41db29): 3 encodings. The word must not assert what the encoding does not do. GEN_OP_FP_MOV is the group of the x87 REGISTER forms -- fld %st(i), fst %st(i), fxch -- which touch no memory and carry no memop row; these three carry one. Naming both groups FP_MOV would erase the one fact that separates them, and the separation is the dataflow-behaviour group a consumer schedules on: an address, a translation, a cache access and a load latency on one side, a register rename on the other. The format widening single->extended is NOT a second operation to lose: extended is x87's only register format, so every x87 FP memory load performs it and it discriminates nothing -- which is why the incumbent does not call it a conversion either (it reserves GEN_OP_FP_CVT for fild, the row below)

fstp m80fp (dbbd80fbffff, db3c24): 2 encodings, the store twin of the fld row. The encoding writes ten bytes of memory and carries a store memop; GEN_OP_FP_MOV asserts a register-to-register move and is false of it. The POP is not the more substantial operation under the substantial-op rule: decrementing the stack top and marking the tag word is bookkeeping that the destination register list already carries (REG_FPSTT, REG_FPTAGS), while the value leaving the register file for memory is what the instruction is for

fxam (d9e5): 1 encoding. It moves nothing -- it reads ST(0), classifies it (NaN, infinity, zero, denormal, unsupported, empty) and writes C0/C2/C3 in the status word. Its destination set contains no data register at all, so GEN_OP_FP_MOV is false on both halves. The dataflow-behaviour group is the one fcom/fucom sit in: inspect an FP operand, produce condition bits, leave every data register alone, and that group's word in this vocabulary is GEN_OP_FP_CMP. That fxam takes one operand where a compare takes two does not move it to another group -- the vocabulary is a bounded generic set and there is no narrower word; an examine and a compare are scheduled on the same path and produce the same kind of result

fnstsw %ax (dfe0): 1 encoding. DF E0 is the AX form: it copies the x87 status word into a general register and performs NO memory access -- the encoding's memop list is empty. GEN_OP_STORE asserts a write to memory, which is the one thing this encoding cannot do, and the incumbent reaches it from the mnemonic's spelling ('store status word') rather than from the operand. The sibling DD /7 fnstsw m16 IS a store and would be scored GEN_OP_STORE correctly; it is not in this corpus. Naming both STORE would erase exactly the distinction between them

fild m32int (db4531): 1 encoding, and it goes the other way from the fld row above on the substantial-op rule. This instruction does two things: it reads four bytes of memory, and it converts a two's-complement integer into binary floating point. The memory access needs no help from the opcode -- the memop rows already publish its address, width and value unconditionally -- but the conversion has no other carrier on the wire, so GEN_OP_LOAD is the reading that loses information and GEN_OP_FP_CVT is the one that loses none. The conversion is also the operation that separates fild from fld: it changes the numeric domain, on a functional unit and at a latency a load does not have, whereas fld's single->extended widening is the load's own delivery format. COVERAGE-PATH, not SETTLED: the tree publishes GEN_OP_LOAD today. REMEDY: give gen_x87's integer memory-load arms the fp.cvt word at the decode site, the same way the x87 control-file words were given theirs; it is a wire change and it is NOT done here

NEG (vector) (a5b8e06e, 63b8e06e): 2 encodings on rule NEG_v. The architecture defines the vector NEG as SUB with a zero first operand and QEMU lowers it through the gvec subtract, so VEC_SUB is a true statement about the operation. GEN_OP_NEG is not: in this vocabulary the VEC_ prefix is what says an operation runs lane-wise on the vector datapath, and GEN_OP_NEG carries no lane structure -- a consumer reading it would size the work as one scalar ALU result where the encoding produces 2, 4, 8 or 16. Losing the lane structure costs more than losing the word 'negate', which the operation's own definition as a subtract-from-zero already implies. There is no GEN_OP_VEC_NEG in the vocabulary to prefer over either, so the choice is between these two and the lane-bearing one wins
